question: You are an unscrubbed nurse walking past a sterile table. What is the safest way to move around it?

question: What is the main difference between a human-made disaster and a natural disaster?

question: Where should a nurse properly document the details after an incident reportable mistake happens?

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of research in nursing?

question: What is the main goal of using a disinfectant on hospital equipment?

question: Why do you need to work with an occupational therapist before a patient gets an automated wheelchair?

question: What is the typical length of a normal adult fallopian tube?

question: Which plant is the natural source of the heart medication digoxin?

question: Why do patients with long-term atrial fibrillation often take blood thinners (anticoagulants)?

question: Why are role-playing and peer education so effective in school health classes?

question: How is BCC different from standard, one-way health talks?

question: A patient with mild arthritis struggles to open childproof medicine caps, so they leave bottles wide open on the table. What is the best nursing advice?

question: What is the correct gap to keep between the top of the crutch and the patient's armpit?

question: What is the main goal of purposive sampling in qualitative studies?

question: What turns raw clinical numbers into useful clinical information?

question: What is the main reason why health insurance is so important for patients?

options.A: To provide free salaries for healthcare workers
options.B: To protect people from high out-of-pocket medical costs
options.C: To generate profits for government agencies
options.D: To completely eliminate all illnesses in a population

explanation: You got this! Health insurance acts as a financial safety net so individuals don't face financial ruin when paying for unexpected medical care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the very first step in the community health decision-making process?

options.A: Evaluate the final outcome
options.B: Allocate available funds
options.C: Develop alternative solutions
options.D: Identify the problem

explanation: You cannot solve an issue until you clearly define and recognize what the actual health problem is using data. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why do hospitals love using cycle menus?

options.A: They provide variety while simplifying food purchasing and kitchen planning
options.B: They ensure that all meals are served at zero financial cost
options.C: They guarantee that every patient eats the exact same food forever
options.D: They allow the kitchen to completely avoid checking food expiration dates

explanation: Cycle menus keep patients from getting bored with food while helping the kitchen budget and buy supplies easily. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T005#GNS227_U3_T005_h4)

question: Which conflict resolution style results in a win-win solution where both parties' needs are fully met?

options.A: Smoothing
options.B: Competing
options.C: Collaboration
options.D: Avoiding

explanation: Collaboration involves open communication and problem-solving to satisfy all concerns, creating a true win-win outcome. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h7)

question: What does REEDA stand for when a nurse checks a healing perineal wound?

options.A: Recovery, Examination, Epithelialization, Diameter, Assessment
options.B: Rubor, Erythema, Edema, Drainage, Alignment
options.C: Redness, Edema, Ecchymosis, Discharge, Approximation
options.D: Rate, Energy, Exudate, Depth, Area

explanation: You've got this! REEDA is our trusty clinical checklist to make sure a perineal tear or episiotomy is healing nicely without infection. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h5)

question: A patient diagnosed with hypertension is struggling to change their eating habits. Which approach best reflects good short-term goal setting?

options.A: Telling the patient to buy an expensive cookbook immediately
options.B: Demanding that the patient stop eating all salt starting today
options.C: Waiting until the blood pressure returns to normal on its own
options.D: Swapping high-sodium canned soups for fresh home-cooked options

explanation: Small, realistic changes like swapping one high-sodium food item represent achievable short-term goals that build lasting habits. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h2)

question: What is the main reason nurses use the Barthel Index assessment tool?

options.A: To diagnose the primary neurological cause of paralysis
options.B: To measure a patient's independence in activities of daily living
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity
options.D: To calculate the exact dosage of pain medication needed

explanation: The Barthel Index is simply a helpful scoring guide to see how well a patient can handle basic tasks like eating, washing, and moving around. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h4)

question: Which Nigerian government agencies help set and enforce rules for environmental health and medical safety?

options.A: Ministry of Finance and Central Bank
options.B: Ministry of Education and Sports
options.C: Federal Ministry of Environment and NAFDAC
options.D: Ministry of Petroleum Resources

explanation: NAFDAC and the Federal Ministry of Environment work together to make sure healthcare facilities keep our environment safe and free from dangerous wastes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h7)

question: Which term describes health services that are affordable and offered at times that are convenient for teenagers?

options.A: Equitable
options.B: Punitive
options.C: Restricted
options.D: Accessible

explanation: Think of accessibility as doors being truly open! It means young people can physically and financially reach the clinic without major hurdles like bad timing. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T18#GNS312_U3_T18_h2)

question: What is the main legal purpose of a patient's nursing care record?

options.A: A temporary shift handover note
options.B: A permanent legal record of care
options.C: A statistical data collection tool
options.D: A personal journal for the nurse

explanation: Great job thinking like a professional! Your notes aren't just paperwork—they stand as official legal proof in court and hospital reviews of the care you gave. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is capitation in the context of HMO operations?

options.A: A cash penalty paid by patients who miss clinic appointments
options.B: A special tax collected from hospital workers
options.C: A fixed regular payment per head made to a primary provider
options.D: The total cost of building a new pharmacy

explanation: Capitation means 'per head,' where the clinic receives a set amount monthly for every registered member, absorbing the risk if they fall sick or gaining if they stay healthy. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why does nursing leadership need to carry out regular program evaluations?

options.A: It reveals if the interventions are actually improving health outcomes
options.B: It ensures that no patient ever complains about the hospital
options.C: It proves that administrative staff are smarter than clinical nurses
options.D: It gives staff a reason to stop working for several months

explanation: Spot on! Evaluation tells us whether our hard work and resources actually solved the health problem we targeted. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h7)

question: What do we call treating mental health conditions using medications like antidepressants and antipsychotics?

options.A: Occupational therapy
options.B: Electroconvulsive therapy
options.C: Milieu therapy
options.D: Pharmacotherapy

explanation: Pharmacotherapy simply means treating health conditions (including psychiatric ones) with prescribed medications. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h7)

question: A patient catches a cold after touching a bedside table that hasn't been cleaned. What kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Droplet transmission
options.B: Airborne transmission
options.C: Indirect contact
options.D: Vector-borne transmission

explanation: Well done! Because the patient touched an object (a fomite) instead of the sick person directly, it's indirect contact. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the main job of the epididymis in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Storage and maturation of sperm
options.B: Production of testosterone
options.C: Secretion of thick mucus
options.D: Filtration of blood waste

explanation: You've got this! Sperm are made in the testes, but they hang out in the epididymis to grow up and learn how to swim properly before they are released. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T5#GNS121_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is a key duty for the community health nurse when dealing with a cholera outbreak?

options.A: Prescribing major surgical procedures for chronic cases
options.B: Managing hospital construction projects in the city
options.C: Educating families on safe water preparation and hygiene
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests on municipal water plants

explanation: As a nurse, teaching families how to boil drinking water, wash hands, and handle food safely is one of our most powerful tools. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T18#GNS313_U2_T18_h7)

question: Why are clinical supervision and peer support so important for nurses working in crisis settings?

options.A: They ensure that nurses never feel empathy for their patients
options.B: They are used primarily to penalize nurses who make charting errors
options.C: They help prevent burnout and address secondary trauma from exposure to crisis stories
options.D: They replace the need for formal psychiatric nursing education

explanation: You cannot pour from an empty cup! Supervision and peer debriefing give you a safe space to offload emotional stress and protect your own mental health. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T1#GNS314_U6_T1_h7)

question: Why does post-disaster communication focus heavily on safe return guidelines and clean water access?

options.A: To train new emergency responders on communication equipment
options.B: To promote local tourism businesses affected by the storm
options.C: To prevent secondary health crises like infections and injuries after the event
options.D: To help insurance companies calculate property values accurately

explanation: Spot on! After a disaster, new risks like contaminated water and damaged buildings pop up, requiring careful guidance to keep people safe. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h3)

question: How is a research report different from a regular story essay?

options.A: It avoids using references or formal citations
options.B: It relies heavily on empirical data and structured formatting
options.C: It is always written in the first person narrative style
options.D: It focuses primarily on fictional clinical scenarios

explanation: Think of a research report as a neat, structured map of proven facts rather than a casual diary entry. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h1)

question: A patient recovered from typhoid fever weeks ago, but lab tests still show they are shedding the bacteria. What type of carrier are they?

options.A: A chronic carrier
options.B: A clinical case
options.C: A healthy carrier
options.D: A convalescent carrier

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Someone who continues to carry and shed germs long after recovering from the illness is known as a chronic carrier. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h2)

question: Even though prolactin levels are high during pregnancy, why doesn't heavy milk production start right away?

options.A: The mammary ducts are completely closed off until the placenta is delivered
options.B: High levels of estrogen and progesterone block the action of prolactin on the alveoli
options.C: The infant must be born to stimulate the release of oxytocin into the bloodstream
options.D: The placenta actively destroys all circulating prolactin until labor begins

explanation: During pregnancy, the placenta produces high levels of hormones (estrogen and progesterone) that act like a temporary 'blocker' on prolactin. Once the placenta is delivered after birth, that block lifts and milk comes in! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h2)

question: A mother feels defensive when asked about her child's diet. What approach should the nurse use?

options.A: Use open-ended, non-judgmental questions to explore current practices
options.B: Hand her a detailed textbook and ask her to read it alone
options.C: Report the mother immediately to the hospital social worker
options.D: Scold the mother so she takes the nutritional advice more seriously

explanation: Empathy goes a long way! Asking open, friendly questions builds trust so mothers feel safe sharing their true feeding challenges. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h8)

question: As a nurse, which common transport mistake should you always avoid?

options.A: Checking patient identification labels against the laboratory request forms
options.B: Wearing clean gloves while handling outside surfaces of specimen tubes
options.C: Assuming standard hospital trash bags are sufficient for off-site transport
options.D: Wiping down secondary containers if a minor drop of fluid touches the outside

explanation: Regular waste bags are not strong enough or certified for road transport. Always use approved UN-certified packaging for safety! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h6)

question: Who usually sits on the management committee for a hospital's Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Elected political leaders from the local government council
options.B: Only senior nursing officers working in the surgical ward
options.C: A multidisciplinary team including pharmacists and accountants
options.D: Only external auditors and private business investors

explanation: It takes teamwork! Managing a DRF needs a mix of clinical, pharmaceutical, and financial experts to keep everything running smoothly and transparently. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h3)

question: A patient experiences a sudden seizure that immediately affects both sides of the brain with a total loss of consciousness. How is this classified?

options.A: Peripheral nerve spasm
options.B: Generalized onset seizure
options.C: Localized partial seizure
options.D: Focal aware seizure

explanation: When both brain hemispheres are engaged from the very beginning, the event is classified as a generalized onset seizure. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h3)

question: What does professional 'accountability' mean for a nurse on duty?

options.A: It shifts all blame for mistakes to the supervising senior nurse
options.B: It requires the hospital management to answer for patient complaints
options.C: It limits the nurse to performing only basic bedside tasks
options.D: It means taking personal responsibility for actions and care outcomes

explanation: Accountability is simply owning your work! When you make a clinical decision or care for a patient, you stand by the results of your actions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why is it important to involve men and boys in community GBV prevention programs?

options.A: To replace international aid workers in distributing food supplies
options.B: To ensure they report all female community members to the police
options.C: To take over all nursing responsibilities inside the local clinic
options.D: To help shift patriarchal attitudes and challenge harmful cultural norms

explanation: Real prevention only happens when men and boys are part of the conversation, shifting old mindsets and helping stop violence at its root. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h9)

question: Why should nurses avoid using judgmental words in patient notes (like 'uncooperative' or 'difficult')?

options.A: They stop the clinic from sending electronic government reports.
options.B: They automatically make the patient chart illegal in court.
options.C: They are unprofessional, biased, and do not provide clear factual evidence of patient status.
options.D: They take up too much physical writing space in the register.

explanation: Stick to the facts! Writing what you actually see and hear ('patient refused medication') is much more professional and legally safe than adding personal opinions. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge when adopting hospital technology in resource-constrained settings?

options.A: Resistance to change from staff used to paper records
options.B: Unstable electricity and power supply disruptions
options.C: Instant availability of unlimited financial budgets
options.D: Data security and patient privacy concerns

explanation: Hospitals rarely have unlimited budgets; funding constraints, power outages, and staff resistance are the real challenges. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why are nursing audits so important for quality assurance?

options.A: They reduce the cost of purchasing hospital medications
options.B: They help discover gaps between standard care and actual practice
options.C: They guarantee that patients will never experience complications
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for physician supervision

explanation: Spot on! By comparing what we actually do against established guidelines, audits show us clearly where our care needs a little extra boost. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h2)

question: How should past studies be presented in a good literature review?

options.A: A random list of book titles found in the library
options.B: Unchecked rumors heard around the hospital ward
options.C: Personal diary entries written by the researcher
options.D: A critical analysis and grouping of past studies by themes

explanation: Instead of just listing past papers one by one, you group them by themes and discuss what they mean together. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses do a 'risk assessment' when they first visit a pregnant woman at home?

options.A: To decide which hospital the baby will attend school
options.B: To find out the exact sex of the unborn baby
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of delivery
options.D: To determine how often the pregnant woman needs monitoring

explanation: Sorting mums by risk helps you know who needs more frequent visits and closer attention. Makes total sense, right? [learn more](GNS225_U3_T4#GNS225_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do nurses need to monitor organ function regularly in patients with systemic autoimmune conditions?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing contagious bacterial infections
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future blood tests
options.C: Widespread inflammation can silently damage vital organs like the kidneys and heart
options.D: It proves whether the patient is following their prescribed diet

explanation: Systemic flare-ups don't just hurt joints—they can quietly cause internal damage over time, making routine checkups a lifesaver. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h6)

question: A sunken fontanelle is most commonly a classic sign of what condition?

options.A: Hydrocephalus
options.B: Skull fracture
options.C: Meningitis
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Correct! When a baby loses body fluids from illness or poor feeding, fluid levels drop and the soft spot dips inward. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T12#GNS121_U6_T12_h6)

question: What is the main goal of health education in nursing?

options.A: Fulfilling mandatory legal paperwork
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment
options.C: Diagnosing complex medical conditions
options.D: Promoting health and preventing disease

explanation: Spot on! Our core job as nurses is to help people stay well and stop illnesses before they even start. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: What should a nurse do FIRST immediately after discovering a medication error has occurred?

options.A: Call the hospital security department to investigate
options.B: Hide the incident report form so nobody finds out
options.C: Leave the ward immediately to avoid disciplinary action
options.D: Assess the patient's clinical condition and provide necessary care

explanation: Patient safety and immediate clinical evaluation always take priority over paperwork or administrative reporting when an error happens. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to protect external validity in clinical research?

options.A: Testing patients only in a hidden laboratory with strict artificial rules
options.B: Conducting the study across multiple different hospitals
options.C: Including patients of various ages and backgrounds
options.D: Using a sample of participants that represents the real patient population

explanation: Overly artificial lab settings make it hard to apply the findings to normal, everyday clinical nursing practice, hurting external validity. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which vaccine is routinely given to newborns to protect against severe forms of childhood TB?

options.A: OPV vaccine
options.B: BCG vaccine
options.C: MMR vaccine
options.D: Tetanus toxoid

explanation: The BCG vaccine is given early in life to give babies strong backup against the most dangerous, widespread forms of childhood TB. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h7)

question: A patient has a leaky mitral valve. Where will blood wrongly flow when the ventricles squeeze?

options.A: Forward into the pulmonary veins
options.B: Forward into the aorta
options.C: Back into the left atrium
options.D: Back into the right ventricle

explanation: Since the mitral valve sits right between the left upper and lower chambers (atrium and ventricle), a weak seal lets blood slip backward upstairs instead of going forward into the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient who previously appeared neat and well-groomed arrives at a follow-up visit looking disheveled with disorganized speech. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A potential worsening of mental status or failing condition
options.B: That the physical assessment is completely unnecessary
options.C: That the patient has changed career paths successfully
options.D: Normal improvement in daily living skills

explanation: Negative changes in personal hygiene and disorganized speech often signal that a patient is relapsing or struggling. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is a major difference between paracetamol (acetaminophen) and NSAIDs?

options.A: Acetaminophen causes significant gastric bleeding
options.B: NSAIDs work exclusively inside the spinal cord
options.C: NSAIDs have no effect on body temperature
options.D: Acetaminophen lacks peripheral anti-inflammatory action

explanation: Both lower fever and ease pain, but paracetamol doesn't fight body inflammation or affect bleeding the way NSAIDs do. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T1#GNS223_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the biggest challenge faced by child-headed households?

options.A: The government evicts them immediately for breaking zoning laws
options.B: Children lack adult guidance, financial stability, and legal protection
options.C: They are required by law to run community health clinics
options.D: They receive too much financial support from international donors

explanation: When young ones live alone without an adult, everyday survival becomes a massive struggle for food, shelter, and safety. Community nurses play a key role in identifying and helping them. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why is an audit trail an important feature in modern EHR systems?

options.A: It blocks patients from viewing their own laboratory tests
options.B: It tracks every user who opens or modifies a patient file
options.C: It calculates the exact cost of medical supplies used daily
options.D: It replaces the need for nurses to give verbal shift reports

explanation: Correct! Audit trails keep everyone accountable by logging exactly who viewed or changed a patient's chart. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary benefit of herd immunity in a community?

options.A: It replaces the need for personal hygiene and clean water
options.B: It completely eliminates all viruses from the global environment
options.C: It protects vulnerable individuals who cannot receive vaccines
options.D: It guarantees that natural infections never occur again

explanation: When enough people are immune, the chain of infection breaks, offering indirect protection to vulnerable, unvaccinated people. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is a major bottleneck when trying to execute the Nigerian health budget?

options.A: Delayed release of approved funds by treasury authorities
options.B: Excessive availability of cash at the primary clinic level
options.C: Automatic approval of all health sector requests
options.D: Complete absence of legislative review

explanation: Even when a budget looks great on paper, getting the actual cash released to clinics often takes a frustratingly long time. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to keep a wide stance and bend their knees when lifting or moving a patient?

options.A: To increase upper body muscular strength instantly
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling nervous or unsteady
options.C: To ensure the patient can place their feet flat on the floor
options.D: To lower the center of gravity and protect the back

explanation: Proper body mechanics with a wide base of support reduces strain on the nurse's lumbar spine during physical maneuvers. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h5)

question: A patient with depression frequently wakes up at 3:00 AM and cannot fall back asleep. What pattern is this?

options.A: Sleep-onset insomnia
options.B: Sleep apnea overlap
options.C: Circadian phase delay
options.D: Early morning awakening

explanation: Waking up way too early and failing to get back to sleep is known as early morning awakening (or terminal insomnia), which is frequently seen in people dealing with depression. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h3)

question: Why must speculums be either single-use plastic or properly sterilized metal?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of infections between patients
options.B: To make the examination completely painless for everyone
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To ensure the equipment feels warm to the patient's touch

explanation: Spot on! Because these instruments touch mucous membranes, keeping them sterile or disposable stops bacteria and viruses from spreading from person to person. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h2)

question: What term describes moving a patient from the surgical ward to the operating theatre within the same hospital?

options.A: Intra-facility transfer
options.B: Elective discharge
options.C: Primary referral
options.D: Inter-facility transfer

explanation: An intra-facility transfer refers to moving a patient between different units or departments inside the same hospital building or compound. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the outermost layer of the skin called?

options.A: Subcutaneous layer
options.B: Dermis
options.C: Hypodermis
options.D: Epidermis

explanation: The epidermis is the outermost, superficial layer of the skin made of epithelial tissue. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h1)

question: How does a work culture of punishment (blame culture) ruin clinical data?

options.A: Staff members spend too much time analyzing charts instead of nursing
options.B: Staff tend to hide mistakes, leading to inaccurate and incomplete data
options.C: Patients refuse to answer questions about their hospital stay
options.D: The hospital is forced to purchase expensive computer software

explanation: If nurses feel they will be punished for mistakes, they'll naturally keep quiet about them. When errors are hidden, our data becomes useless for fixing real problems. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h5)

question: When is chemical disinfection most commonly used in a healthcare facility?

options.A: For treating liquid infectious waste and laboratory cultures
options.B: For packaging expired patient food trays
options.C: For disposing of heavy metal surgical instruments
options.D: For processing large wooden crates and office furniture

explanation: Liquid waste and lab cultures are often treated directly with chemical disinfectants to make them safe before they go down the sewer lines. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: Studying a rare medical condition, a researcher asks early patients to connect her with other patients they know. What technique is this?

options.A: Snowball sampling
options.B: Quota sampling
options.C: Stratified sampling
options.D: Systematic sampling

explanation: Spot on! Just like a snowball rolls and gets bigger, your participant list grows as each person refers you to the next. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h4)

question: What primary farming challenge do mountainous regions usually face?

options.A: Absence of any sunlight during the year
options.B: Excessive flat land and too much rainfall
options.C: Constantly flooded river basins
options.D: Steep slopes and short growing seasons

explanation: High altitudes have rocky, steep land and shorter periods of warm weather, making it tough for crops to grow. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h2)

question: Why is the role of a food handler particularly critical in a hospital environment?

options.A: Hospital patients eat more frequently than people outside
options.B: Hospital kitchens prepare larger quantities of food than standard restaurants
options.C: Hospital patients often have weakened immune systems that make them vulnerable to infections
options.D: Hospital food handlers are required to have medical degrees

explanation: Vulnerable patients in healthcare facilities suffer severe complications from foodborne illnesses that healthy people might overcome easily. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: How does the World Wide Web relate to the internet?

options.A: It is an older offline system replaced by the internet
options.B: It is a standalone computer used only by doctors
options.C: It is a specific service that displays web pages using the internet
options.D: It is the physical wire running underneath hospital floors

explanation: The web is just one part of the internet, acting as a collection of pages and sites viewed through a browser. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h1)

question: How does family planning directly promote gender equality?

options.A: By making biological differences between men and women disappear
options.B: By giving women control over their reproductive lives so they can pursue education and work
options.C: By ensuring that only women make decisions regarding community finances
options.D: By legally prohibiting men from participating in healthcare discussions

explanation: Fertility control frees women from the cycle of constant childrearing, enabling them to pursue personal and professional goals on equal footing. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: What is one of the biggest challenges to using tele-health in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Unreliable electricity and internet connectivity
options.B: Zero demand for healthcare services
options.C: Excessive availability of trained tele-nurses
options.D: An overabundance of smartphones

explanation: Power cuts and poor network signals remain common hurdles that make smooth virtual care tricky in some areas. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h6)

question: A recovering leprosy patient feels very depressed because people in the community are avoiding them. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise them to pack up and relocate to another state
options.B: Assure them that people will soon forget about it
options.C: Offer a listening ear and connect them with a support group
options.D: Tell the patient never to discuss their illness with anyone

explanation: Emotional support and connecting with others who understand are powerful ways to beat stigma and heal the mind. You're going to be a wonderfully empathetic nurse! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is a major sign that a coping behavior is maladaptive rather than helpful?

options.A: It always improves personal relationships
options.B: It appears only once in a person's life
options.C: It is rigid and impairs daily functioning
options.D: It easily resolves without any outside help

explanation: Maladaptive habits are stuck on repeat. Instead of helping you solve a problem, they cause rigid roadblocks that make daily life and relationships harder. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why should you avoid twisting your body while carrying a heavy load?

options.A: It causes the rescue team to lose their sense of direction
options.B: It increases the air pressure inside the transport vehicle
options.C: It automatically makes the patient slide off the stretcher
options.D: It places excessive rotational stress on the lumbar spine disks

explanation: That's correct! Twisting while carrying something heavy is one of the fastest ways nurses hurt their lower backs. Protect your spine! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h5)

question: What is the main job of the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical brain circuit in OCD?

options.A: Controlling voluntary muscle movement in the upper extremities
options.B: Producing visual images during rapid eye movement sleep
options.C: Filtering sensory information and regulating behavioral habits
options.D: Regulating body temperature and fluid balance in the kidneys

explanation: You nailed it! When this pathway has trouble filtering routine signals, the brain gets stuck in repetitive loops of thoughts and actions. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the main psychological feature of illness anxiety disorder (hypochondriasis)?

options.A: Complete lack of awareness regarding bodily changes
options.B: Intentional simulation of physical disease for attention
options.C: Frequent hallucinations involving internal organ failure
options.D: Excessive anxiety about having a serious illness

explanation: You've got this! The core thing to remember here is constant, overwhelming worry about having a severe medical condition, even when medical tests show everything is fine. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h1)

question: What key right must be explicitly explained to participants before they enter a prospective study?

options.A: The obligation to pay for any specialized diagnostic tests
options.B: The requirement to remain in the project until final publication
options.C: The promise that no adverse events will ever occur
options.D: The right to withdraw from the study at any time without penalty

explanation: Voluntary participation means individuals can exit a research study whenever they choose without losing access to standard medical care. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h6)

question: A ward introduces hourly rounds to stop patient falls. Tracking whether the nurses actually completed those hourly rounds is an example of what?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Baseline measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Outcome measure

explanation: Spot on! A process measure simply checks whether the specific steps or tasks in our care plan are actually being carried out day-to-day. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is a major problem for hospitals when national economic funding is low?

options.A: Surplus funding for specialized nursing research
options.B: Excessive availability of advanced medical technology
options.C: Immediate reduction in patient admission rates across all wards
options.D: Severe shortages of basic supplies and heavy workloads

explanation: You've probably seen this in practice: low funding means fewer gloves, less medication, and exhausted staff carrying heavy workloads. You are doing great learning about this! [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h3)

question: How does water's polarity help keep our bodies running?

options.A: It provides a dense source of stored glucose calories for hard work
options.B: It builds rigid structural amino acid chains inside human bone
options.C: It acts as a universal solvent that dissolves and transports vital nutrients
options.D: It prevents minerals from entering the bloodstream during digestion

explanation: Because water is polar, it easily dissolves and carries important chemicals and nutrients to every part of the body. Excellent! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T004#GNS227_U1_T004_h7)

question: What does 'growth faltering' look like on a child's growth chart?

options.A: A steady upward curve parallel to reference lines
options.B: Measurements that stay above the median line
options.C: A sudden increase in height over one month
options.D: A flat or downward-sloping growth curve

explanation: Growth faltering happens when weight gain slows down or stops entirely, making the growth line flatten out or dip downwards. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h6)

question: A researcher creates a survey for anxiety, but the questions actually measure physical hunger. What is wrong with this tool?

options.A: Validity
options.B: Sample size
options.C: Secondary source status
options.D: Reliability

explanation: Validity is about whether your tool measures what it claims to measure. If it measures hunger instead of anxiety, its validity is off! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a thorough home safety assessment?

options.A: Observing how the client moves through hallways and rooms
options.B: Checking household lighting and walking pathways
options.C: Ignoring family dynamics and focusing strictly on the medical diagnosis
options.D: Reviewing medication storage and expiration dates

explanation: Family members and caregivers play a huge role in home safety. Leaving them out gives you an incomplete picture of the client's care. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h8)

question: How do electronic records make a nurse's daily work easier compared to old paper charts?

options.A: By shortening the required length of a hospital stay for surgery
options.B: By eliminating the need to ever measure patient vital signs
options.C: By reducing medication errors caused by poor handwriting
options.D: By removing all documentation duties from the nursing staff

explanation: Great job! We've all struggled to read messy handwriting. Digital records clear that up so nobody gives the wrong drug by mistake. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h1)

question: A patient is scheduled for a hysterosalpingography (HSG). What is the most important preparatory action for the nurse to take?

options.A: Administer a cleansing enema to empty the entire colon
options.B: Explain the procedure steps and what kind of cramping sensation to expect
options.C: Instruct the patient to fast from solid food for twenty-four hours
options.D: Place an indwelling urinary catheter before the imaging begins

explanation: Preparation is all about calming nerves! Explaining what will happen and warning them about mild period-like cramps helps the patient feel safe and ready. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h8)

question: How long should you rub your hands together with an alcohol-based sanitizer?

options.A: 5 full minutes
options.B: 5 to 10 seconds
options.C: 20 to 30 seconds
options.D: 2 full minutes

explanation: You got it! Giving it 20 to 30 seconds ensures the sanitizer covers every part of your hands and kills the germs effectively. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of adding chlorine during water treatment?

options.A: To kill remaining pathogenic microorganisms
options.B: To settle heavy sand particles to the bottom
options.C: To make the water taste sweet and fresh
options.D: To remove dissolved iron and copper

explanation: Disinfection agents like chlorine are used at the final stages to destroy any remaining bacteria, viruses, or parasites. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the proper technique for cleaning a patient's skin before giving an injection?

options.A: Use a circular motion starting from the center and moving outward.
options.B: Clean from the outer edges inward toward the exact puncture spot.
options.C: Wipe back and forth rapidly across the site with a dry gauze pad.
options.D: Apply warm soapy water and rinse with sterile tap water.

explanation: Well done! Starting from the center and swirling outwards pushes germs away from the exact spot where the needle will pierce the skin. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of an intrinsic (internal) risk factor for a patient?

options.A: An improperly calibrated infusion pump
options.B: Muscle weakness from advanced age
options.C: A wet floor in the hallway
options.D: Poor lighting in the patient room

explanation: Intrinsic risks come from inside the patient's own body, like age-related muscle weakness, rather than from things around the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the single biggest risk factor for breast cancer that you cannot change?

options.A: Engaging in sedentary office work
options.B: Being female and advancing in age
options.C: Living in a densely populated city
options.D: Consuming a high-fat urban diet

explanation: Simply growing older and being a woman carry the highest statistical risk. It's totally unmodifiable, but knowing it helps us target our screening! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h3)

question: How does long-term fear and stress affect a patient's physical healing?

options.A: It speeds up tissue repair and lowers blood glucose.
options.B: It has no measurable impact on physical recovery.
options.C: It impairs wound healing and suppresses the immune system.
options.D: It completely stops the need for pain medication.

explanation: You're correct! High stress hormones like cortisol hang around during prolonged fear, which slows down tissue repair and weakens immunity. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h7)

question: Where should a nurse begin looking for a suitable vein for initial cannulation?

options.A: Most distal areas of the upper extremities
options.B: Delicate veins directly over wrist joint creases
options.C: Large veins located in the lower extremities
options.D: Proximal veins close to the upper shoulder

explanation: Starting low on the hand or forearm preserves higher vein sites for future access if the current line fails. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is accurate data collection so important for evidence-based nursing?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing hospital equipment
options.B: It eliminates the need for nurses to document patient vital signs
options.C: It ensures clinical decisions are based on solid proof rather than guesswork
options.D: It guarantees that every patient will recover without complications

explanation: Good evidence keeps our patients safe! Accurate data gives us the real facts we need instead of just guessing what works. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h1)

question: As a nurse entering a brand new community, what should always be your very first step?

options.A: Listening to the community before telling them what to do
options.B: Demanding that the village head build a new health post
options.C: Distributing medications without proper medical evaluations
options.D: Issuing strict rules on sanitation and personal hygiene

explanation: Brilliant! Listening first shows respect. It helps you understand their everyday realities and priorities before you try to introduce any changes. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by PHC development committees in Nigeria?

options.A: Poor financial record-keeping
options.B: Lack of transport for community outreach
options.C: Excessive, surplus funding with no way to spend it
options.D: Political interference in local appointments

explanation: Committees almost always suffer from underfunding and resource scarcity rather than having too much money. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h6)

question: A resident says they already took their morning blood pressure pill, but the medication administration record (MAR) is blank for that time. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer a second dose immediately to ensure their blood pressure stays controlled
options.B: Wait until the evening shift to see if the blood pressure spikes
options.C: Assume the resident is correct and sign the record as given by the resident
options.D: Withhold the dose and consult the prescribing physician or charge nurse before acting

explanation: Brilliant! Giving a double dose can be dangerous. Always pause, check the facts, and consult your senior colleagues or doctor when something doesn't match up. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h5)

question: Why use liquid chemical sterilants instead of an autoclave for delicate instruments?

options.A: Chemical sterilization leaves a protective coating that prevents rust
options.B: Steam sterilization destroys all microbial spores less effectively
options.C: Chemicals are much cheaper and faster than running steam sterilizers
options.D: The instruments are heat-sensitive and would melt or warp in an autoclave

explanation: Things like fiber-optic scopes and delicate plastics can't handle extreme autoclave heat, so low-temp chemical baths save the day! [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h4)

question: A nurse in a rural Nigerian clinic notices more waterborne diseases during the rainy season. What action best reflects PHC philosophy?

options.A: Wait inside the clinic and only treat patients who manage to walk in with severe diarrhea
options.B: Collaborate with community leaders to organize safe water education and promote simple water boiling methods
options.C: Complain to the federal government and refuse to see any more sick patients
options.D: Refer every single patient immediately to a foreign overseas hospital

explanation: Spot on! Being proactive with education and community teamwork stops outbreaks at the grassroots before they overwhelm the clinic. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h6)

question: You are getting ready to repair a perineal tear after delivery. Which drug should you draw up to numb the area?

options.A: Lidocaine
options.B: Hydralazine
options.C: Ergometrine
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: You got it! Lidocaine is our go-to local anesthetic for numbing the perineum before doing a repair or episiotomy. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why do people lose weight so fast in the first few days of a strict fad diet?

options.A: Instantaneous healing of the gastrointestinal lining
options.B: Permanent destruction of abnormal fat cells in the abdomen
options.C: Loss of body water and breakdown of stored muscle protein
options.D: Rapid increase in physical activity levels induced by supplements

explanation: That quick drop on the scale isn't fat—it's mostly water weight and muscle glycogen being used up. Good to know as a future nurse! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h4)

question: What brings people together in a community of identity or orientation?

options.A: Working for the same commercial transport company
options.B: Living within the exact same municipal boundary line
options.C: Shared values, faith, culture, or life experiences
options.D: Sharing a temporary emergency shelter after a flood

explanation: You nailed it! It's heart and culture—beliefs, traditions, and life experiences—that bond these groups together, not just physical land. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is a major duty of a Community Health Officer (CHO) at a primary health center?

options.A: Supervising junior health workers and managing clinic operations
options.B: Auditing national health ministry financial records
options.C: Performing major surgeries in rural theater suites
options.D: Manufacturing essential pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Well done! CHOs act as great leaders at the facility level, keeping everything organized and guiding the team to deliver wonderful care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h2)

question: A nurse is examining a child with suspected paralytic polio. What is a key physical sign to look for?

options.A: Gradual ascending paralysis starting in the feet
options.B: Painful joint swelling and localized skin rashes
options.C: Symmetrical rigid spasms and hyperactive reflexes
options.D: Asymmetrical muscle weakness and absent reflexes

explanation: Well done! Polio typically causes floppy weakness on one side more than the other (asymmetrical) along with missing reflexes in those limbs. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h3)

question: Which type of reservoir includes people who carry an infection without showing any signs or symptoms?

options.A: Human reservoirs
options.B: Fomite reservoirs
options.C: Environmental reservoirs
options.D: Animal reservoirs

explanation: Spot on! Asymptomatic human carriers walk around feeling totally fine while unknowingly passing germs along to others. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h2)

question: What is the main goal of doing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA)?

options.A: To prove that the hospital equipment never breaks down
options.B: To uncover the underlying system flaws that led to an error
options.C: To speed up the discharge process for injured patients
options.D: To find a specific staff member to punish for the mistake

explanation: An RCA is like detective work! It digs past simple human slip-ups to find the deep operational causes behind an error. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h4)

question: A hospital introduces a system that allows bedside nurses to help make decisions about clinical care standards. What concept does this show?

options.A: Rigid top-down command
options.B: Decentralisation and empowerment
options.C: High mechanistic control
options.D: Strict work specialisation

explanation: When bedside nurses get a voice in clinical decisions, power is shared downward. That is a great example of decentralisation and staff empowerment! [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h7)

question: A weak patient is learning to walk down the hallway and needs a little extra support to stay steady. What should you use?

options.A: A mechanical hoist
options.B: A slide sheet
options.C: A ceiling lift
options.D: A gait belt

explanation: You're doing great! A gait belt goes snugly around the patient's waist, giving you a safe and secure grip to steady them as they walk. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why does the biopsychosocial model work best for explaining drug addiction?

options.A: It focuses solely on the patient's current environmental stress
options.B: It looks at biological, psychological, and social factors together
options.C: It relies entirely on psychiatric medication history
options.D: It proves that genetics is the only true cause of drug use

explanation: Addiction is complex, and the biopsychosocial model acknowledges that body chemistry, mental health, and life surroundings all contribute. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h4)

question: A patient tells you: 'My chest feels tight since this morning.' Where should you document this exact statement?

options.A: Discharge planning and social history
options.B: Objective physical examination findings
options.C: Past medical history and surgical background
options.D: Chief complaint and history of present illness

explanation: Active symptoms that patients report themselves always go right into the chief complaint and history of present illness sections. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h2)

question: Where does a newborn usually pick up the germs that cause ophthalmia neonatorum?

options.A: From the maternal birth canal during delivery
options.B: Via airborne droplets in the delivery room
options.C: From direct skin contact with nursery staff
options.D: Through contaminated formula feeding equipment

explanation: Exactly right! As the baby passes through the birth canal, they can come into contact with maternal infections. It's why routine eye care at birth is so vital. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h2)

question: What is the purpose of binding the chest with cloth after applying heat during breast ironing?

options.A: To hold medicinal herbal leaves in place
options.B: To absorb sweat from the heated stones
options.C: To keep the chest warm during cold weather
options.D: To physically restrict future breast growth

explanation: Tight binding is used alongside heat to prevent the breast tissue from expanding outward. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h3)

question: What happens in passive surveillance?

options.A: Patients must call a special hotline to report their own illness.
options.B: Health workers actively visit every household in the village.
options.C: Data is only collected during a national census every ten years.
options.D: Clinics send routine reports without being pushed by health officers.

explanation: Think of passive surveillance as your local clinic doing what they normally do—sending in their regular reports as part of daily duty without waiting for someone to chase them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h3)

question: When should suction be applied as you insert the catheter into the artificial airway?

options.A: Never apply suction while inserting the catheter
options.B: Apply continuous suction the entire time you push it in
options.C: Apply suction only when the catheter hits the back of the throat
options.D: Apply suction in short bursts on the way down

explanation: Applying suction during insertion damages the delicate lining of the airway and removes helpful air; suction is only applied while withdrawing. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: A post-op patient presses a handheld button on their IV machine to release a safe dose of pain meds. What is this device called?

options.A: Enteral feeding pump
options.B: Large Volume Pump
options.C: Insulin ambulatory pump
options.D: Patient-Controlled Analgesia pump

explanation: That's right! A PCA pump lets patients safely manage their own pain within strict limits set by the care team. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h2)

question: How do touchless gesture controls help nurses working in sterile environments like the operating room?

options.A: They eliminate the need for patient identification wristbands
options.B: They make computer screens brighter in dark surgical suites
options.C: They allow computers to run without needing any electricity
options.D: They let nurses interact with software without breaking sterile technique

explanation: Brilliant! Gesture controls let you check screens and records with a wave of your hand, keeping your sterile gloves clean and safe. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h8)

question: Why is it important to check up on your patient after giving an injection or IV medication?

options.A: It ensures the medication achieved its intended effect and checks for adverse reactions.
options.B: It proves to the hospital pharmacy that the correct vial was opened.
options.C: It satisfies legal billing requirements for injectable supplies.
options.D: It replaces the need to check vital signs prior to administration.

explanation: You nailed it! Because injections work fast, following up helps you catch any early side effects and make sure the patient is feeling better. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h8)

question: Why does the spinal cord have a thicker area called the cervical enlargement?

options.A: To protect the delicate blood vessels entering the skull
options.B: To manage sensory and motor input for the upper limbs
options.C: To anchor the spinal cord firmly to the thoracic cage
options.D: To produce extra cerebrospinal fluid for the brain

explanation: Think of it this way: your arms need a lot of wiring! The spinal cord bulges out in the neck and lower back regions because it has to handle all the heavy nerve traffic going to and from your limbs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h1)

question: Why does early marriage still happen in many places even though laws ban it?

options.A: Lack of interest from international organizations
options.B: Automatic exemption of rural communities from laws
options.C: Universal agreement among traditional rulers
options.D: Strong influence of local customs and poverty

explanation: Traditions and financial hardship are the main reasons why this practice continues, even when the law says otherwise. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why can't a nurse just focus on pure biology (like lab tests and vitals) when caring for a mental health patient?

options.A: Psychological symptoms have no connection to physical health at all
options.B: External life events and social pressures deeply affect emotional well-being
options.C: Doctors rarely pay attention to physical lab results during admission
options.D: Biological tests are too expensive to run in most local clinics

explanation: You got it! A patient's daily struggles, relationships, and environment heavily shape their mental health. We treat the whole person, not just the lab results. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h1)

question: What substance is put into a vaccine to trigger the body's immune defense?

options.A: An antibiotic
options.B: A red blood cell
options.C: A plasma protein
options.D: An antigen

explanation: Great job! Vaccines carry harmless pieces of germs called antigens. This teaches your immune system what the real germ looks like without making you sick. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h1)

question: During early blood loss, what is the body's main goal to protect itself?

options.A: Slower heart rate to save energy
options.B: Increase urine production to flush toxins
options.C: Maintain blood supply to the brain and heart
options.D: Keep the skin warm and well-perfused

explanation: In early shock, the body smartly shunts blood away from less critical areas to protect VIP organs like the brain and heart. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why is maintaining the 'cold chain' so crucial for vaccines?

options.A: To prevent the vials from freezing solid
options.B: To preserve vaccine potency and effectiveness
options.C: To stop bacteria from growing on the outside of bottles
options.D: To make the injection less painful for infants

explanation: Exactly! Vaccines are delicate biological products. Without the proper temperature, they lose their power to protect patients. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h5)

question: What is the main reason nurses get professional malpractice insurance?

options.A: To cover personal medical bills during a workplace illness
options.B: To guarantee a higher salary within hospital settings
options.C: To replace the need for an active nursing license renewal
options.D: To provide financial protection against legal claims of professional negligence

explanation: Malpractice insurance is there to protect you from the huge financial stress of lawsuits if a mistake or negligence is claimed. You've got this! [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why does adjusting to a dark room take much longer than adjusting to bright light?

options.A: Rod pigments take time to regenerate in the dark
options.B: Blood flow to the retina stops temporarily
options.C: The pupil takes hours to dilate fully
options.D: The cornea must change its thickness overnight

explanation: Your eye's light-sensitive chemicals take a little while to rebuild after being bleached by light. Patience is key, both in exams and in learning! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h6)

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial check to make *before* a patient goes for a liver biopsy?

options.A: Check that clotting blood tests are safe and consent is signed
options.B: Perform a minor surgery to drain belly fluid
options.C: Give them strong general anesthesia right in the ward
options.D: Make sure they eat a large heavy meal

explanation: Spot on! Safety first—always verify clotting labs and make sure the patient understands and signs the consent form before the procedure. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h3)

question: A patient cannot read the written instructions for taking their blood pressure medication. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Scold the patient for not attending school and refusing to learn English
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately without any further medication instructions
options.C: Write the instructions in complex medical terminology for clarity
options.D: Use simple verbal explanations, pictorial charts, and involve a trusted family caregiver

explanation: Wonderful! Using pictures, clear talking points, and family help ensures the patient understands their medication safely. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T15#GNS312_U4_T15_h7)

question: Which type of measure tells us the final, ultimate impact of care on the patient's health?

options.A: Control measure
options.B: Outcome measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Process measure

explanation: Brilliant! An outcome measure looks at the final result—how the patient is actually feeling and recovering after our care. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h2)

question: A nurse checks a client's chart to see if their symptoms have lasted long enough to meet clinical guidelines. Which manual is she likely using?

options.A: The DSM-5-TR
options.B: The International Nursing Index
options.C: The Hospital Safety Manual
options.D: The British Pharmacopoeia

explanation: The DSM-5-TR gives exact timelines and severity checklists that clinicians use to match a client's symptoms. You're mastering psychiatric tools! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T3#GNS314_U2_T3_h3)

question: A patient with high blood pressure loves strongly salted local seasonings. What is the most practical nursing approach?

options.A: Prescribe an expensive imported meal plan from another continent
options.B: Suggest reducing the salt gradually and using local aromatic herbs for flavor
options.C: Ignore their diet since salt intake has no effect on blood pressure
options.D: Tell the patient they must never taste local soup again for the rest of their life

explanation: Offering realistic tweaks like local herbs for flavor respects their food preferences while protecting their heart health. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h7)

question: What must a nurse obtain from a community member before conducting an individual health interview or examination?

options.A: Informed consent
options.B: Written tax records
options.C: A financial deposit
options.D: Political clearance

explanation: Every participant has the right to know what a study involves and agree voluntarily before giving personal data. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why must surgical instruments be wiped free of blood right after a procedure finishes?

options.A: To ensure the instruments weigh less when returned to central supply
options.B: To prevent the circulating nurse from wearing heavy utility gloves
options.C: To keep blood from drying and damaging the instruments during sterilization
options.D: To make it easier for the surgeon to count them before leaving

explanation: If blood dries up in the tiny joints and crevices, it ruins the instruments and makes later cleaning much harder. Quick wiping keeps them in top shape! [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h7)

question: Which immune cells are on the front lines, patrolling tissues to destroy abnormal cells?

options.A: Albumin and globulin proteins
options.B: Eosinophils and basophils
options.C: Red blood cells and platelets
options.D: T-cells and natural killer cells

explanation: You got it! T-cells and natural killer (NK) cells are the heavy lifters of the immune system, constantly hunting down and destroying abnormal or infected cells. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why can predictive formulas (like the Harris-Benedict equation) sometimes be misleading for critically ill patients?

options.A: They measure direct body heat rather than gas exchange
options.B: They require the patient to be placed inside a sealed heat chamber
options.C: They only provide estimates and may miscalculate actual needs during severe illness
options.D: They can only be used on healthy newborn infants

explanation: Formulas use averages for healthy people. But when a patient has severe burns or trauma, their body behaves unpredictably, so formulas can miss the mark. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h5)

question: How do most patients typically approach HIV disclosure?

options.A: By printing flyers and distributing them in the local market
options.B: By refusing to ever tell anyone under any circumstance
options.C: Selectively, by telling specific trusted individuals over time
options.D: By announcing it publicly to their entire workplace on day one

explanation: Disclosure is usually a gradual, graded process where patients share their status only with carefully chosen people. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of routine spirometry testing in an industrial occupational health clinic?

options.A: To test the employee's hearing capacity against machine noise
options.B: To check if the worker has contracted a stomach ulcer
options.C: To measure the exact body weight and fat percentage of workers
options.D: To detect early drops in lung function before symptoms appear

explanation: Regular spirometry allows nurses and occupational health officers to spot early breathing impairments so corrective safety steps can be taken immediately. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h8)

question: A patient comes to the surgical ward with a suspected knee injury involving a torn ligament. Which diagnostic test is the nurse most likely to prepare the patient for?

options.A: Routine urinalysis
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Standard chest X-ray
options.D: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

explanation: Ligaments are soft tissues inside a joint, making MRI the ideal test to check for tears. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h3)

question: A nurse notices a sudden jump in malaria cases during the rainy season. What kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Foodborne
options.B: Waterborne
options.C: Vector-borne
options.D: Airborne

explanation: Spot on! Malaria is spread by mosquitoes (the vector), which love to breed in the puddles formed during the rainy season. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h2)

question: How does severe malnutrition negatively impact a community's immune status?

options.A: It directly destroys the skin's physical ability to sweat
options.B: It prevents infants from absorbing breast milk antibodies
options.C: It speeds up the rate at which vaccines expire in storage
options.D: It impairs the body's ability to produce antibodies and immune cells

explanation: Nutrients are the building blocks of the immune system; lacking them stops the body from making enough cells and antibodies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h6)

question: What kind of information do you mainly gather when taking a patient's health history?

options.A: Subjective data from the patient
options.B: Quantitative data from vital signs
options.C: Measurable signs from physical exams
options.D: Objective data from laboratory tests

explanation: Spot on! A health history is all about what the patient tells you they are feeling. That makes it subjective data. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h1)

question: What does Evidence-Based Practice primarily combine in clinical decision-making?

options.A: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient preferences
options.B: Pharmaceutical advertisements and medical textbook theory
options.C: Traditional habits, personal opinions, and trial-and-error
options.D: Hospital budget reports, doctor orders, and insurance rules

explanation: True evidence-based practice brings together solid research findings, the nurse's professional experience, and the values of the patient. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It can only be performed on hospitalized surgical patients
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to analyze
options.C: It measures body fat percentage instead of food intake
options.D: It relies heavily on the patient's memory and honesty

explanation: Patients can easily forget what they ate or misjudge portion sizes, which can make your dietary data a bit off. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for a small skin biopsy is panicking because they are sure it means they have cancer. How should the nurse reply?

options.A: Confirm that the doctor strongly suspects a malignant tumor
options.B: Suggest that the patient cancel the procedure until they feel calmer
options.C: Tell the patient not to worry because skin problems are never serious
options.D: Explain that biopsies are done to check many different conditions, not just cancer

explanation: It's totally normal for patients to worry about the 'C-word.' Gently reminding them that biopsies check for simple rashes, fungus, and routine infections too can be a huge relief. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T3#GNS213_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the best way to organize the body of a literature review?

options.A: By the alphabetical order of the authors' first names
options.B: By the physical weight of the textbooks referenced
options.C: By the exact length of each published journal article
options.D: By themes, trends, or logical subtopics

explanation: Structuring your paper by themes lets you easily compare what different authors say about the same specific subtopic. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why does the nurse occasionally tap the side of the medication cup during the procedure?

options.A: To prevent the plastic parts from overheating while the compressor runs
options.B: To help remaining liquid droplets slide down into the bottom of the cup to be aerosolized
options.C: To signal to the patient that the treatment session is halfway finished
options.D: To clear any dust blocking the outside air filter vents

explanation: Tapping the cup drops clinging fluid back into the reservoir so it doesn't go to waste on the walls. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h5)
